testName: Class B Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What does the application pressure gauge show?

options.text: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
The temperature of air in the braking system.
The pressure of air coming from the compressor.
How many times the brakes have been used.

questions.correctAnswerText: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
questions.explanation: The application pressure gauge in an air brake system shows how much air pressure is being applied to the brakes. Not all air brake systems have this gauge.

questions.question: What do leaking shock absorbers mean?

options.text: This is a potentially dangerous problem.
This will break the turn signals.
This is safe if you only drive on highways.

questions.correctAnswerText: This is a potentially dangerous problem.
questions.explanation: The suspension system keeps a vehicle's axles in place. Damaged parts like leaking shock absorbers can be dangerous defects.

questions.question: Why are roads most slippery right after rain starts?

options.text: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
Gravel washes to the middle of the lane.
Some tires are not made for rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
questions.explanation: When rain first starts, water mixes with oil drippings on the road. This creates a slippery and dangerous mixture.

questions.question: When checking the engine compartment, what should you do?

options.text: Do not engage the parking brake.
Block the wheels so they cannot move.
Put the gearshift in first gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Block the wheels so they cannot move.
questions.explanation: Before checking the engine compartment, turn on the parking brakes and block the wheels. Check the engine before starting it.

questions.question: Which crime does NOT disqualify someone from getting a hazardous materials endorsement?
questions.explanation: Kidnapping, smuggling, and immigration violations disqualify someone for seven years. More serious crimes like murder result in lifetime disqualification. Speeding does not disqualify someone.

questions.question: How do you use the stab braking method in an emergency?

options.text: Press the brakes fully until the wheels lock, release until they roll, then repeat.
Press the brakes halfway while keeping the wheels rolling.
Press the brakes fully and hold them down until the vehicle stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the brakes fully until the wheels lock, release until they roll, then repeat.
questions.explanation: The stab braking method means pressing the brakes fully until they lock. Release the brakes until the wheels start rolling, then repeat this process.

questions.question: ____ is a thin layer of ice on road surfaces.
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. You can see the road through it, so it looks like the road is just wet.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop if your brakes fail while driving downhill?

options.text: Let the vehicle slow down on its own.
Use rumble strips to slow down.

questions.explanation: If your brakes fail on a hill, find an escape ramp to stop. If no ramp is available, drive into an open field or side road that goes uphill or flattens out.

questions.question: How soon must you tell your employer about a traffic violation conviction?
questions.explanation: You must tell your employer about any traffic violation conviction within 30 days. This does not include parking violations.

questions.question: What should you do when transporting cargo?

options.text: Check the load and securing devices within the first 50 miles.
Do not use mirrors to look behind.
Hold a cell phone in your hand for emergencies.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the load and securing devices within the first 50 miles.
questions.explanation: Check cargo and securing devices before you start. During the trip, check them within the first 50 miles, every three hours or 150 miles, and after every break.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a vehicle inspection report?

options.text: It tells the motor carrier about problems that need fixing.
It makes sure the vehicle is inspected regularly.
It makes drivers responsible for inspecting their vehicles.
It plans the next five trips.

questions.correctAnswerText: It tells the motor carrier about problems that need fixing.
questions.explanation: A vehicle inspection report lets drivers tell the motor carrier about issues that could affect safe driving. Drivers should fill out a report after each day of driving. They should note any problems that could affect vehicle safety or cause a breakdown.

questions.question: When parked on the side of the road, you should:

options.text: Use only the rear flashing lights.
Use one set of turn signals.

questions.explanation: Turn on your four-way emergency flashers if you park on the side of the road. This is very important when driving at night.

questions.question: When the brake pedal is pushed down, air brakes work:

options.text: Only when it is warm outside.

questions.explanation: Air brakes do not work instantly because air takes time to travel through the brake lines. There is a delay of at least half a second between when you press the brake pedal and when the brakes begin to work.

questions.question: Service brakes should:

options.text: Only be tested by a trained mechanic.

questions.explanation: Always check that your service brakes work well before you drive. Testing the brakes before each trip helps you find problems before you need to brake on the road.

questions.question: How can you avoid becoming drowsy on a trip?

options.text: Get about three hours of sleep beforehand.

questions.explanation: To reduce drowsiness while driving, get seven to eight hours of sleep before the trip. Drive during hours when you are normally awake. Plan to take breaks during the trip. Exercise regularly.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, you may be asked to:

options.text: Pull forward into a parking space.

questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test may include straight line backing, offset back/right parking, offset back/left parking, driver side parallel parking, conventional parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: A tank endorsement is:

options.text: Needed when transporting both liquids and gases.

questions.correctAnswerText: Needed when transporting both liquids and gases.
questions.explanation: You need a tank endorsement to drive a tank vehicle that transports liquids or gases. This applies to both hazardous and non-hazardous materials.

questions.question: Alcohol can be removed from your system:
questions.explanation: Your liver removes alcohol from your body at a fixed rate. The only way to sober up is to give your body time to remove the alcohol naturally.

questions.question: Drivers can get traveler information by dialing what number on their phone?
questions.explanation: Dial 511 on your phone to access free traveler information. The system gives updates about crashes, travel times, traffic, lane closures, severe weather, construction, and emergency evacuation information on Florida highways and roads.

questions.question: If an emergency vehicle is stopped on the side of a two-lane, two-way road, approaching drivers must:

options.text: Move to the left half of the lane.
Travel at least 20 mph below the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Travel at least 20 mph below the posted speed limit.
questions.explanation: Florida's Move Over Law requires you to slow down to at least 20 mph below the posted speed limit when approaching an emergency vehicle stopped on the side of a two-lane road.

questions.question: If your engine catches fire, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Turn off the engine right away.
Spray foam from under the vehicle.

questions.explanation: If your engine catches fire, turn off the engine right away. Do not open the hood. Instead, spray foam through the openings or from under the vehicle.

questions.question: When backing up, what is best to do?

options.text: Use only the mirror on the passenger's side.
Back up as fast as you can.
Turn toward the passenger's side when possible.
Use a helper if you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use a helper if you can.
questions.explanation: When backing up, go slowly and use both mirrors. If possible, have a helper watch your blind spots. You and your helper should agree on a signal that means "stop."

questions.question: What does the suspension system do?

options.text: Supports the vehicle and everything in it.
Keeps cargo the right distance behind the driver.
Keeps the right distance between vehicles.
Makes the tires carry less weight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Supports the vehicle and everything in it.
questions.explanation: The suspension system supports the vehicle and its cargo while keeping the axles in position. A damaged suspension system is very dangerous.

questions.question: What can very hot temperatures cause?
questions.explanation: Hot air expands, which increases tire pressure. Too much pressure can cause a tire to fail. Check your tire pressure often when driving in hot weather.

questions.question: If a traffic light has been green for a long time, what will probably happen?

options.text: It will stay green as you get closer.
It will change from green straight to red without yellow.

questions.explanation: If a traffic light has been green for a long time, it will likely turn yellow soon. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: About headlights, which is true?

options.text: You usually don't need them when driving at night.
They shine brighter than the sun.

questions.explanation: Use high beam headlights at night when it is safe and legal. However, high beams can blind other drivers. Switch to low beams when you are within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle.

questions.question: What does the air compressor governor control?

options.text: When air gets pumped into the storage tanks.
How fast air gets pumped into the storage tanks.
The temperature of the air in the storage tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: When air gets pumped into the storage tanks.
questions.explanation: In an air brake system, the air compressor governor decides when air should be pumped into the storage tanks.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, where should weight go?
questions.explanation: Load cargo as low as possible in the trailer. Heavy cargo placed too high can cause the vehicle to tip over.

questions.question: When double clutching, if you stay in neutral too long and can't shift to the next gear, what should you do?

options.text: Stop the vehicle and start over.
Return to neutral, release the clutch, speed up, and try again.
Skip the gear and go to the next one.

questions.correctAnswerText: Return to neutral, release the clutch, speed up, and try again.
questions.explanation: If you stay in neutral too long and can't shift, don't force it. Return to neutral, release the clutch, speed up the engine to match road speed, and try again.

questions.question: How do states make sure a CDL or CLP driver has only one license?

options.text: They use a computer system that connects all states.
They look through the driver's wallet.

questions.correctAnswerText: They use a computer system that connects all states.
questions.explanation: All U.S. states share CDL and CLP license information in a computer database. When you apply for a license, the state checks this database to make sure you don't already have a license in another state.

questions.question: What do air tank drains do?

options.text: Let rain water enter the tanks.
Remove water and oil from the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove water and oil from the tanks.
questions.explanation: Air brake system tanks have drains to remove water and compressor oil. If water and oil build up in the system, they can damage the brakes.

questions.question: When checking under your vehicle for leaks, which fluid do you NOT need to look for?
questions.explanation: Before a trip, check under your vehicle for leaks of fresh oil, coolant, grease, or fuel.

questions.question: When checking the exhaust system, how should it be?
questions.explanation: Check that the exhaust system has no loose, broken, or missing parts.

questions.question: What must all air tanks have?
questions.explanation: Air brake tanks must have drain valves. These valves remove oil and water buildup and can be operated manually or automatically.

questions.question: What is the maximum air loss allowed for a single vehicle with air brakes during a leakage test?
questions.explanation: A single vehicle with air brakes should lose no more than 3 psi in one minute during a leakage test.

questions.question: How should you change lanes?

options.text: Move quickly before other vehicles enter the lane.
Move slowly in case another vehicle is in the lane.
Do not use your turn signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move slowly in case another vehicle is in the lane.
questions.explanation: Change lanes slowly and smoothly. This gives other drivers time to move out of your way or warn you. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: When does hydroplaning usually happen?

options.text: Where water sits on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where water sits on the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens where water collects on the road. Low tire pressure or worn tread makes it more likely. Hydroplaning can occur at speeds as low as 30 mph if there is enough water on the road.

questions.question: Which of these is acceptable during a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: Front tire tread of 2/32 of an inch

questions.explanation: Front tires must have at least 4/32 inch tread depth. Other tires need at least 2/32 inch. Tires must not be worn, cracked, or unequal in size. They must have proper air pressure. Tires from different makers are acceptable.

questions.question: Which surface has the least traction?
questions.explanation: Be very careful when driving on melting ice. Wet ice is much more slippery than dry ice.

questions.question: What are placards?

options.text: Warning signs on vehicles showing cargo hazards
A type of tire for snowy weather

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning signs on vehicles showing cargo hazards
questions.explanation: Placards are diamond-shaped warning signs placed on vehicles carrying hazardous materials. They identify the specific type of hazard in the cargo.

questions.question: What is the maximum air leakage rate for a triple combination vehicle with air brakes during a static leakage test?
questions.explanation: A triple combination vehicle with air brakes should leak no more than 5 psi of air per minute during a static leakage test. If air leaks faster than this, the vehicle needs repair and should not be driven.

questions.question: Why should your mirrors show both the road behind you and part of your vehicle?

options.text: Showing only the road in the mirrors makes drivers carsick.
Part of the truck in the mirrors gives you a point of reference.
It is against the law to show only the road.
You need to see reflections of vehicles on the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Part of the truck in the mirrors gives you a point of reference.
questions.explanation: You should see part of your vehicle in your mirrors. This helps you judge how close other vehicles and objects are to your truck.

questions.question: What should you do when you encounter a railroad crossing during the driving test?

options.text: Pass another vehicle on the tracks if it is moving slowly.
Change lanes while on the tracks.
Do not change gears while on the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not change gears while on the tracks.
questions.explanation: During the driving test, do not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is on the railroad tracks.

questions.question: What task may be included in a basic vehicle control skills test?

options.text: Pull forward into a parking space.

questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test may include straight line backing, offset back/right parking, offset back/left parking, driver side parallel parking, conventional parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: Why should you do pre-trip inspection steps in the same order each time?

options.text: You will be less likely to forget a step.
The form must be followed in order.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will be less likely to forget a step.
questions.explanation: Using the same order each time helps you learn the steps. A routine makes it less likely that you will skip or forget a step.

questions.question: How long must carriers keep fuel records that support IFTA quarterly fuel tax returns?
questions.explanation: Commercial vehicles operating in interstate commerce must follow IFTA (International Fuel Tax Agreement) rules. Carriers must keep fuel and mileage records that support IFTA quarterly tax returns for four years.

questions.question: What should you do when driving through a curve during the skills test?

options.text: Leave your lane if needed to complete the curve.
Reduce your speed after entering the curve.
Do not check for other vehicles while turning.
Reduce your speed before entering the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed before entering the curve.
questions.explanation: Slow down before you enter a curve. Reduce your speed enough so you do not need to brake or shift gears in the curve. Stay in your lane and keep checking for traffic in all directions.

questions.question: When making tight maneuvers, what should a driver do?

options.text: Open the door for a better look.

questions.explanation: Always check your mirrors regularly while driving. Check them especially often when changing lanes, turning, merging, or making tight maneuvers.

questions.question: What should you do when backing?

options.text: Move quickly to get out of the way of other drivers.
Try not to use your mirrors.

questions.explanation: Backing a large commercial vehicle is dangerous because you cannot see everything behind you. If you must back up, use a helper when possible.

questions.question: If you notice a safety or mechanical problem while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Stay quiet and hope the problem goes away.
Write a report describing the problem.
Try to fix the issue yourself.
Do not use that part and hope others do not notice.

questions.correctAnswerText: Write a report describing the problem.
questions.explanation: At the end of each day of driving, write a report about any vehicle problems. Note any issues that could affect safety or cause the vehicle to break down.
